questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Glucose is added to $1$ litre of water to such an extent that $\Delta T_f/K_f$ equals to $\dfrac{1}{1000}$. The weight of glucose added is
questions.solution:
Using the formula for depression in freezing point:

$\Delta T_f = K_f \times m$

where $m$ is the molality of the solution.

Given $\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_f} = \dfrac{1}{1000}$

Therefore, $m = \dfrac{1}{1000}$ mol/kg.

Mass of $1$ litre of water is $1$ kg.

Molality $m = \dfrac{\text{Moles of solute}}{\text{Mass of solvent in kg}}$

Moles of glucose $= \dfrac{1}{1000} \times 1 = 10^{-3}$ mol.

Molar mass of glucose $(C_6H_{12}O_6)$ is $180$ g/mol.

Weight of glucose added $= 10^{-3} \times 180 = 0.18$ gm.

Answer: $0.18$ gm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The van't Hoff Factor (i) for a dilute aqueous solution of $Na_2SO_4$ is
questions.solution:
The dissociation of $Na_2SO_4$ in an aqueous solution is given by:

$Na_2SO_4 \rightleftharpoons 2Na^+ + SO_4^{2-}$

Let the initial number of moles of $Na_2SO_4$ be $1$ and the degree of dissociation be $\alpha$.

Moles at equilibrium:
$Na_2SO_4 = 1 - \alpha$
$Na^+ = 2\alpha$
$SO_4^{2-} = \alpha$

Total number of moles at equilibrium $= 1 - \alpha + 2\alpha + \alpha = 1 + 2\alpha$

The van't Hoff factor $i$ is the ratio of the total number of moles of particles at equilibrium to the initial number of moles.

$i = \dfrac{1 + 2\alpha}{1} = 1 + 2\alpha$

Answer: $1 + 2\alpha$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Equal weights of ethane and hydrogen are mixed in an empty container at 25 C. The fraction of total pressure exerted by hydrogen is
questions.solution: Given, equal weights of ethane and hydrogen are mixed in an empty container at $25^{{}^{\circ}} $$\mathrm{C}$$ Initial gram weight $=$\begin{array}{ll}\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6} & \mathrm{H}_{2} \\ \mathrm{Wg} & \mathrm{Wg}\end{array}$ Number of moles $=$$\frac{w}{30}$ \quad $\frac{w}{2}$ According to Henry's law, $\begin{array}{l}\frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{p_{\text{total }}}=\chi_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}=\frac{n_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{n_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}+n_{\mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{H}_{6}}}=\frac{\frac{w}{2}}{\frac{w}{2}+\frac{w}{30}} \\ \frac{p_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{p_{\text{total }}}=\frac{\frac{w}{2}}{\frac{15 w+w}{30}}=\frac{w}{2} \times \frac{30}{16 w}=\frac{15}{16}\end{array}$ So, the fraction of total pressure exerted by hydrogen is 15: 16

questions.q: To observe an elevation of boiling point of $0.05^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C},$ the amount of a solute (mol. wt. $=100$ ) to be added to $100 \mathrm{g}$ of water $\left(K_{b}=0.5\right)$ is
questions.solution: Elevation of boiling point, $\Delta$ T_{b}=$\frac{w \times K_{b} \times 1000}{M \times W} ($ Here, w and $W=$ weights of solute and solvent respectively. $M=$ molecular weight of solute and $K_{b}=$ constant On substituting values, we get of $\begin{aligned}0.05 &=\frac{W \times 0.5 \times 1000}{100 \times 100}$\\ w &=$\frac{0.05 \times 100 \times 100}{0.5 \times 1000}=1 \mathrm{g} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The measured freezing point depression for a $0.1 \mathrm{m}$ aqueous $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}$ solution is $0.19^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. The acid dissociation constant $K_{a}$ at this concentration will be (Given, $K_{f}$ the molal cryoscopic constant $=1.86 \mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \Delta T_{f} &=i \times K_{t} \times m \\ \therefore & i=\frac{\Delta T_{f}}{K_{t} \times m}=\frac{0.19}{1.86 \times 0.1}=1.02 \end{aligned}$ Again from, $\alpha=\frac{i-1}{n-1}=\frac{1.02-1}{2-1}=0.02=2.0 \times 10^{-2} \begin{aligned}\text{$ for $} \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COOH}& \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{COO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}^{+}\\ K \mathrm{a}&=\mathrm{C} \alpha^{2}\\ &=0.1 \times\left(2 \times10^{-2}\right)^{2} \\ \text{ and } =4 \times10^{-5} \end{aligned}$

Molality of NaCl solution $=\frac{n}{W} \times 1000=\frac{58.5}{W_{\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}}} \times 1000=\frac{1000}{\mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{M}_{2}} \mathrm{O}}$
Molality of $f \mathrm{C}_{6} \mathrm{H}_{1} \not \mathrm{O}_{6}$ solution = $\frac{\frac{180}{180} \times 1000}{w_{\mathrm{H}_{2}} \mathrm{O}}\frac{1000}{W_{M_{2}} O}$. Both the solutions have same molarity but the values for $\mathrm{NaCl}$ and glucose are ${2}$ and 1respectively. $\left.\therefore \quad \Delta T_{b(\mathrm{NaG})}=2 \times \Delta T_{b C C_{6} H_{1} 2} \mathrm{O}_{6}\right)$
